subject: Deploy mode prioritization & dedicated GPU sizing — WaveHealth
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Tess O'Leary <tess.oleary@wavehealth.ai>, Alan Chu <alan.chu@wavehealth.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Nov 2027 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo recap: deploy-mode prioritization + sizing asks

Hi Tess / Alan —

Thanks for the time today. Short recap plus the asks we discussed so we can size a Dedicated path cleanly (and map tradeoffs vs Hosted / Private):

Summary of customer priorities (from the call):
- Primary need: low-latency user-facing inference for conversational triage; strict P95 latency target (~<250ms) on short queries.
- Throughput profile: mix of many short queries and a smaller percent of long generation jobs for summaries.
- Data residency: US-only environment; potential PHI scope for a subset of traffic.
- Procurement timeline: procurement kicked off, target pilot in ~6–8 weeks.

Where we need specifics to recommend Dedicated SKU(s):
1) TPS targets (sustained vs peak) — what sustained qps/requests-per-second would you plan for?
2) Token mix: avg tokens per short query and avg length for long jobs (sample prompt examples would help).
3) Latency SLO (p95) and how frequently you can accept slightly higher tail latency during spikes.
4) Isolation needs: single-tenant reserved pool vs multi-tenant dedicated (isolated v. shared) and encryption/KMS requirements.

Immediate Redwood proposal (high-level):
- If you need strict isolation and PHI handling -> Dedicated Private VPC with customer KMS.
- If you prioritize speed-to-market and lower ops -> Hosted API to validate prompt shapes, then migrate to Dedicated for the pilot.
- For Dedicated sizing we typically model 3 SKU candidates: H100 cluster (best throughput for short tokens), A100 80GB (balanced), and A100 40GB (cost-efficient but limited memory for long-gen).

Next steps:
- Attached: wave_capacity_workbook_v1.xlsx — please populate the TP S and token examples in the "Traffic" tab.
- Tess: if you can share a representative set of 25 short prompts + 10 long-generation prompts we can baseline token shapes and produce a GPU-concurrency recommendation.
- I'll loop in infra (Ben) and solutions (Neha) for a short sizing run and we can propose a few Dedicated pool options and cost estimates.

Attachments: wave_capacity_workbook_v1.xlsx, SOC2_questionnaire_wave.pdf

Thanks — talk soon.

—Michael

Date: Mon, 08 Nov 2027 18:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: deploy-mode prioritization + sizing asks

Thanks Michael — quick clarifications from our side:

- Traffic profile: our target for the first pilot is ~120 RPS sustained (this is user-facing queries); peak observed from demo load can spike to ~320 RPS for short bursts (90th percentile days).
- Token mix: short queries average 18–35 tokens (mostly intent/classification + short reply). Long jobs (nightly summarization/batch) average ~700–1,200 tokens per generation; those are not latency-sensitive (can be processed off-peak).
- Latency: p95 target ~250ms for short queries; p99 can be relaxed during spikes but we'd like to see an estimate.
- Isolation / compliance: PHI will be present in <5% of requests initially; we need a Dedicated pool with VPC & KMS for pilot if possible.

Two asks:
1) Can you confirm whether Dedicated supports per-customer isolated pools (single-tenant) vs reserved multi-tenant capacity?
2) Do you have a rough guidance on which GPUs to prioritize for this mix (we care about average cost/TPS and ability to handle occasional long generations without running out of memory).

I'll attach our initial SOC/security questionnaire (shortlist) — procurement will follow up with contractish items.

Best,
Tess

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Nov 2027 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo recap: deploy-mode prioritization + sizing asks

Ben / Neha — forwarding WaveHealth clarifications. Key points they gave: 120 RPS sustained, spikes ~320 RPS, short tokens ~18–35, long gen 700–1200 tokens, PHI in <5% of requests and they want Dedicated VPC + KMS for pilot.

Proposed internal approach:
- Run a quick sizing model with three SKU hypotheses: H100 (best short-token throughput + headroom), A100 80GB (compromise), A100 40GB (cheapest footprint).
- Model assumptions: short-query token length 25 tokens avg, average response tokens 12, concurrency target driven by sustained RPS at target p95 250ms. Use continuous batching and KV prefix caching for repeat prefixes.
- Deliverables: 1) estimated GPUs needed for sustained/peak, 2) estimated concurrency slots, 3) cost delta across SKUs, 4) potential fallback options (hosted fallback for overflow).

Can you run a quick back-of-envelope and we’ll present 2 recommended configurations (cost-optimized and performance-optimized) to Tess + procurement?

—Michael

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Nov 2027 11:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-demo recap: deploy-mode prioritization + sizing asks

Quick back-of-envelope based on their shapes:
- Assumptions: short path 25 tokens in / 12 tokens out avg = 37 tokens total per short request; long path average 900 tokens total for generation. Traffic split ~90% short / 10% long.
- For H100 (with optimized kernels + int8 where applicable): ~6,000 short requests/sec per GPU? (this is optimistic — more realistic sustained is 1,500–2,500 RPS per GPU depending on batching window and KV cache effectiveness). For planning use ~2,000 RPS per H100 for their mix. -> For sustained 120 RPS they are tiny relative to H100 capacity; focus is p95 latency, not raw throughput.
- Concurrency: to keep p95 <250ms at sustained 120 RPS, estimate ~6–8 concurrency slots with low batching; for spikes to 320 RPS we should allow autoscale headroom to 20–30 slots or overflow to Hosted.
- Memory: long jobs (900 tokens) push memory — prefer A100 80GB or H100 if they want single-GPU long-gen without offloading; A100 40GB may require model sharding/long-gen fallback.

Recommendation (for pilot):
- Performance-focused: 1 H100-backed Dedicated pool with autoscale to 3 instances (gives headroom for spikes, best p95).
- Cost-focused: 2x A100 80GB with aggressive batching + cache; fallback to Hosted for spikes > sustained capacity.

I can produce a short worksheet with cost estimates and a modeled p95 curve if you want — recommend we ask for sample prompts and a 48-hour traffic capture (or synthetic trace).

—Ben
